jurisdictions.name: Ghana

royalties.name: Mineral royalty: Minerals and Mining (Royalties) Regulations, 2025 (L.I. 2517), gold (non-small-scale mining operations)
royalties.price_unit: US$/oz: weekly average LBMA London PM fix for the month's gold sales
royalties.notes: rate_pct is null because the rate is price-linked; apply the band (schedule wording 'Above X - Y', so upper bound inclusive). Small-scale gold has a separate 2% rate. Gazette notification 19 Dec 2025; in force 10 Mar 2026 (one report says 9 Mar). Replaced the flat 5% royalty: 'The fixed rate of 5% with royalty bands for gold and lithium have been abolished.' The flat 5% was the rate at the 1 Jan 2026 valuation date. Reportedly not applied to holders of a valid stability or development agreement fixed before the L.I.; a new lease pays the sliding scale. Royalty is due within 15 days after month end, on revenue from sales. A secondary source says 'a minimum of 5% royalty where gold price is below $2000'; the schedule text shows 5% only up to US$1,900.

royalties.name: Growth and Sustainability Levy (GSL)
royalties.notes: 1% of gross production. The GSL (Amendment) Act 2026 was passed on 13 Mar 2026; TaxLawGH reports it was assented to and gazetted as Act 1166 on 31 Mar 2026. It cut gold miners from 3% back to 1% and applies the 1% to mining and upstream petroleum companies generally. At the 1 Jan 2026 valuation date gold miners paid 3%. Quote (GhTaxClub news, https://ghtaxclub.com/news/ghana-reduces-gsl-on-mining-companies-from-3-to-1/, via search): 'The Government has now decided to revert to the original 1% for all mining and upstream petroleum entities.'

source.quote: It will reduce the levy imposed on gold mining companies from three per cent to one per cent of gross production.

royalties.name: Mineral royalty: L.I. 2517, lithium (spodumene)
royalties.price_unit: US$/t spodumene concentrate. The market value is set by the parties at arm's length, having regard to international prices. No reference grade is stated, so SC6 is an assumption.
royalties.notes: SOURCES CONFLICT; the schedule page itself was not read. 'bands' follows summaries of the regulation (WTS Global, TaxLawGH) and Ecofin's Dec 2025 report. 'alt_bands_ewoyaa_reports' follows smallcaps.com.au's Mar 2026 report of the ratified Ewoyaa lease; Bloomberg (20 Mar 2026) and Reuters (via Mining Weekly and CNBC Africa) also put the 12% threshold at US$3,200, and a promotional Kodal piece (Oct 2026) says the 1,500/2,300/3,200 schedule is binding and 'earlier proposals used different breakpoints'. SC6 at US$2,501-3,000/t = 10% in every version. SC6 at US$3,001-3,200/t = 12% under 'bands' but 10% under the alt bands. Also, US$2,301-2,500 = 7% vs 10%. In Dec 2025 the Lands Minister said lithium was at 7% under then-current prices (quote: 'lithium attracts a royalty rate of 7%, which could rise to as much as 12% if prices increase significantly'). Before 10 Mar 2026 the lithium lease rate was 10% flat (original Ewoyaa lease).

other_sources.quote: The framework sets the royalty at 5% when prices are at or below $1,500 per ton, 7% for prices between $1,501 and $2,500 per ton, 10% between $2,501 and $3,000 per ton, and 12% for prices above $3,000 per ton.
The Schedule applies rates of 5%, 7%, 10% or 12%, depending on the lithium-spodumene price band stated in the instrument.
other_sources.note: Search summaries of this page give the bands as 5% up to US$1,500/t, 7% to 2,500, 10% to 3,000, 12% above 3,000. Valuation text from the regulation as surfaced by search: 'For the purposes of calculating royalties on lithium (spodumene) the market value of the lithium (spodumene) obtained pursuant to a mining operation shall be determined by the p[arties...]'

other_sources.quote: Royalties now range from 5% for spodumene priced up to US$1,500/t, escalating to 7% between US$1,500 and US$2,300/t, then 10% from US$2,300 to US$3,200/t, and reaching 12% for prices above US$3,200/t.
It will range from 5% when the price for concentrate is below $1,500 a ton to 12% if it exceeds $3,200
once prices move beyond US$2,500, which gives us 10 percent, any rise above US$3,000 will attract up to 12 percent
other_sources.note: Lands Minister quoted when the L.I. was laid.

other_sources.quote: following the expiration of the 21-sitting-day review period, a new Legislative Instrument, Minerals and Mining (Royalty) Regulations, 2025 ... has become legally binding
other_sources.note: Atlantic Lithium RNS. Also: 'All other fiscal terms outlined in the October 2023 Mining Lease remain unchanged.'

corporate_tax_pct.notes: Minerals Commission page, possibly dated 2023. Ghana Chamber of Mines FAQ (Dec 2025, https://ghanachamberofmines.org/storage/2025/12/Ghana-Chamber-of-Mines-FAQs.pdf, via search): 'However, mining companies with an Investment or Development Agreement have a CIT rate of 32.5%.'

mining_tax.desc: No separate profit-based mining tax was identified. The production levy is the GSL at 1% of gross production (3% for gold miners until 31 Mar 2026), listed under royalties.

state_carry_pct.quote: (1) Where a mineral right is for mining or exploitation, the Government shall acquire a ten percent free carried interest in the rights and obligations of the mineral operations in respect of which financial contribution shall not be paid by Government.
state_carry_pct.notes: Act 703 s.43(1). Copies also at faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/gha85046a.pdf and repository.parliament.gh; the search did not say which copy the quote came from. No statutory option to buy more was found (null). EWOYAA (Atlantic Lithium): the lease granted in Oct 2023 gives the state a 13% free carry, and the ratified lease keeps it. The Ministry is quoted at https://thebusinessexecutive.net/atlantic-lithium-mining-lease-terms-best-for-ghana-minister/: 'He had also said there had been an increase in state free carried interest from 10 per cent to 13 per cent.' Ecofin (Dec 2025): 'the revision leaves intact other key terms of the original lease, including the state's free equity stake'. One report gives 19% in total (13% free carry plus 6% held by MIIF). Mining Weekly dates ratification 20 Mar 2026; Accra Street Journal says 19 Mar. Graphic Online's report on the Barari DV lithium lease mentions a 12% free carried interest; that may refer to Barari DV, not Ewoyaa.

dividend_wht_pct.quote: dividends are subject to income tax at the dividend WHT rate of 8%
dividend_wht_pct.notes: The quote may be the search tool's paraphrase of PwC. Another guide, as returned by search: 'an 8% withholding tax is imposed on dividends paid to resident shareholders and nonresident shareholders unless an exemption or treaty applies'.

jurisdictions.notes: Terms for a new mine producing in 2026: L.I. 2517 sliding-scale royalty, plus GSL 1%, plus CIT 35%, plus 10% free carry, plus 8% dividend WHT. At the 1 Jan 2026 valuation date the rules differed: flat 5% royalty and 3% GSL for gold. L.I. 2517 (Minerals and Mining (Royalties) Regulations, 2025): laid 19 Dec 2025, in force 10 Mar 2026 after 21 sitting days. GhTaxClub also hosts a Dec 2025 version (https://ghtaxclub.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/MINERALS-AND-MINING-ROYALTY-REGULATIONS-2025-GhTaxCLub-1.pdf), which may differ from the gazetted text. Atlantic Lithium is subject to a pending Huayou takeover (announced May 2026).

jurisdictions.name: Mali

royalties.name: Taxe ad valorem (TAV) / royalty: Mining Code Law No. 2023-040 and implementing Decree No. 2024-0396/PT-RM
royalties.notes: UNRESOLVED; the decree text was not read. Ecofin (c. Oct 2025) gives a price-linked scale from the implementing decree, with no rate stated for US$1,000-1,600/oz or above US$2,500 (left null). Conflicting reports: Daily Beirut (https://dailybeirut.com/en/world/mining-companies-mali-face-pressure-rising-royalties-insecurity/): 'the rate ranges between 3% and 8% depending on the ounce price, with the possibility of increasing it by 0.5 to 1 percentage point whenever the price exceeds the $2,000 level'. DiscoveryAlert, Sep 2026 (https://discoveryalert.com/analysis/mali-gold-investment-risk-reopening-september-2026/): '...including the 35% mandatory state equity stake and the 10.5% gold royalty rate'. That may be an all-in figure; it is unverified. Unattributed excerpts: 'jumping from 6.5% to 10%' and 'around 10.5% of the value (up from around 6%)'. Do not use for production without Decree 2024-0396.

source.quote: According to an implementation decree of the 2023 mining code, a royalty of 3% applies when gold trades below $1,000 per ounce. This rate climbs to 6% between $1,600 and $2,000 per ounce, then to 7% up to $2,500.

royalties.notes: Not found: no copper rate surfaced for the 2023 Code.

royalties.name: TAV / royalty (lithium)
royalties.notes: No lithium rate found. UNCTAD says the implementing decree gives the government priority in permit allocation for 'strategic minerals' such as lithium and uranium. Kodal's Bougouni MoU: the State of Mali and national private investors hold 35% of LMLB combined, KMUK 65% (search paraphrase of https://kodalminerals.com/operations/bougouni-lithium-project/).

source.quote: there is currently no specific legislation targeting energy-transition minerals like lithium, cobalt, rare earths or copper

mining_tax.desc: Not established. Mali Actuel says the code sets a modular royalty rate by substance and degree of processing, and that a decree fixes the TAV calculation and the rates of the overproduction and surface royalties. One unattributed excerpt (possibly discoveryalert.com, 'How Mali's Mining Revenues Are Funding a $900M Infrastructure Drive') reads: 'mandatory contributions from mining permit holders: 1% of quarterly turnover plus an ad valorem levy of 1% for the first five years, rising to 2% thereafter'. It is unverified and not used.

state_carry_pct.quote: the State's initial interest in Fekola Regional is maintained at 10%, but the State may acquire up to an additional 20% interest, and a further 5% interest must be available to be acquired by a local Malian stakeholder
state_carry_pct.notes: Free carry is 10%, with an option for up to 20% more; UNCTAD and mining.com put the option window at the first two years of commercial production. A further 5% is reserved for Malian private investors, for up to 35% in total. A second excerpt, as returned by search: 'The state holds a free 10% share in all mining projects, with the option to purchase an additional 20% equity stake for a total potential shareholding of 30%' ... 'a 5% stake can be ceded to locals, taking state and private Malian interests in new projects to 35%, and certain tax exemptions have been abolished.' B2Gold's 7 Aug 2026 release gives Fekola Regional as 65% B2Gold / 35% State.

jurisdictions.notes: Mining Code: Law No. 2023-040 of 29 Aug 2023 (Official Journal 1 Sep 2023), repealing Ordinance 2019-022. Quote (ENS, https://www.ensafrica.com/news/detail/9042/mining-legislation-reform-in-mali-strengtheni, via search): 'The new Code repeals Ordinance No. 2019-022/P-RM of 27 September 2019 and has been supplemented by Implementing Decree No 2024-0396/PT-RM of 9 July 2024.' The decree was adopted by the Council of Ministers on 3 Jul 2024; its PDF is on mines.gouv.ml and was not read. Local content law: No. 2023-041, same date. Application to new permits: B2Gold's Menankoto exploitation permit (Aug 2026) was issued under the 2023 Code, while Fekola stays under the 2012 Code (search paraphrase of https://www.b2gold.com/news-media/news-releases/news-details/2026/B2Gold-Granted-Fekola-Regional-Exploitation-Permit-by-the-State-of-Mali/default.aspx). Kodal says Bougouni is compliant with the 2023 Code. Not found: the TAV rates by mineral, the special tax on certain products (ISCP), CIT and dividend WHT.

jurisdictions.name: Côte d'Ivoire

royalties.name: Taxe ad valorem (gold), raised by the 2025 Annexe fiscale (Loi de finances n° 2024-1109 du 18 décembre 2024)
royalties.notes: Each band rose 2 points, effective 10 Jan 2025: 3 to 5, 3.5 to 5.5, 4 to 6, 5 to 7, and 6 to 8. Source of each band: the 1,000 and 1,300 bounds are in the annex excerpt; the 1,300-1,600 band is from Deloitte; the annex summary moves the 1,600-2,000 tier to 7%; 8% is the fifth, top band of the list. No excerpt shows the words 'above US$2,000' for that band. Mining Code art. 164 stability does not protect against these revisions; quote (Mines Actu / annex, via search): 'les dispositions de l'article 164 du Code minier relatives à l'intangibilité du régime fiscal et douanier ne s'appliquent pas aux révisions des taux prévus par l'annexe fiscale 2025'. Gold has been above US$2,000, so miners pay 8% in practice; Reuters via Kitco (16 Dec 2025, https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2025-12-16/ivory-coast-miners-start-paying-higher-royalties-after-failed) reports the 8% applied retroactively to Jan 2025 after a dispute. No mining measure was found in the 2026 annex (Loi n° 2025-987 du 19 déc. 2025). PENDING, not in force at the valuation date: Bloomberg (20 Nov 2026, https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-20/ivory-coast-to-raise-mineral-royalty-rates-before-imf-talks) reports a plan to lift the mineral royalty to 9.5% from 6% and the mining-area local contribution to 3% from 0.5%, as part of a mining-code overhaul. One analysis says a revised gold scale reaches 12% only above US$6,000/oz. The 2027 tax annex was before parliament in Nov 2026.

royalties.name: Redevance proportionnelle (gold): Decree 2023-1454 of 27 Oct 2023, as revised by the decree signed 25 Mar 2025

bands.note: No source states this band; applying Ecofin's +1 point per US$500 rule would give 9%, but that is not recorded.

step_rule.text: The rate rises by one percentage point for every additional $500 increase beyond that range.

royalties.notes: Bands up to US$2,000 are from the Oct 2023 decree, as quoted by Mines Actu. Whether the Mar 2025 decree changed them is not confirmed. 2,000-3,000 = 7% (Mar 2025 decree, Mines Actu). 3,000-3,500 = 8% (Ecofin, Feb 2026: https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-industry/0202-52481-higher-gold-prices-lift-burkina-faso-s-revenue-from-sanbrado-by-67-in-2025). Quote (Bullionworld, https://bullionworld.in/documents/news/DtGold2_083126.html, via search): 'Burkina Faso reaching 10 per cent between USD 4,000 and USD 4,500 per ounce'. Quote (Miningmx, https://www.miningmx.com/news/gold/67212-gold-rally-lifts-west-african-resources-royalty-bill/, via search): '7% between $2,000/oz and $3,000/oz, rising by one percentage point for every US$500 increase in the gold price above $3,000/oz.' No cap reported. Base: proportional royalty on value; the exact base wording was not seen.

source.quote: le décret a été signé avec les taux suivants : 3% si le cours de l'or est inférieur à 1.000 dollars/l'once, 4% si le cours est compris entre 1.000 et 1.300 dollars/l'once, 5% lorsqu'il est compris entre 1.300 et 1500 dollars l'once, 6% si le cours de l'once d'or est compris entre 1500 et 1700 dollars/l'once, 6,5% si le cours est compris entre 1700 et 2000 dollars/l'once et 7% si le cours est supé[rieur] ... le gouvernement a révisé le décret qui a été signé le 25 mars 2025. mining_tax.desc: Not established. The 2024 Code sets by regulation the share of proportional royalties paid into the Fonds minier de développement (art. 28); no rate was found. Priority dividend to the State: West African Resources said its payment 'has become non-discretionary' (WAF's subsidiary declared a priority dividend equal to 15% of retained earnings to end-2024).

state_carry_pct.quote: It also allows the State to own a further contributing shareholding interest (up to 30% (thirty percent)) in the same mining company, or to allocate it to the "national private sector".
state_carry_pct.notes: Law No. 016-2024/ALT of 18 Jul 2024 raised the free carry to 15% (from 10%). Quote (via search, from https://volterrafietta.com/client-alert-burkina-fasos-new-mining-code-increased-state-control-and-domestic-participation/ or a similar summary): '15% free-carried state interest, meaning the government receives the stake without paying for it'. The further contributing interest of up to 30% (up to 45% in total) may go to the national private sector. The mining-registry director called a 35% request on Kiaka 'a solicitation – it is not forcing' (Mining Weekly, 5 Sep 2025). 'many provisions of the new Mining Code cannot be implemented, because they are dependent on the drafting and approval of implementation regulations.'

jurisdictions.notes: Mining Code: Loi n° 016-2024/ALT du 18 juillet 2024, replacing Loi 036-2015/CNT as amended by Loi 012-2023/ALT (energie-mines.gov.bf). The Oct 2023 decree lifted the 2017 decree's 5% cap ('l'ancien décret, celui de 2017, avait plafonné le taux de perception des royalties à 5%, si le cours de l'or dépasse 1500 dollars l'once').

Ghana lithium (L.I. 2517) thresholds conflict. Summaries of the regulation (WTS Global, TaxLawGH) and Ecofin (Dec 2025) give 5% to US$1,500/t, 7% to 2,500, 10% to 3,000, and 12% above. Post-ratification reports on Ewoyaa (smallcaps.com.au, Mar 2026; Bloomberg and Reuters, 20 Mar 2026) put 12% only above US$3,200; smallcaps gives 7% to 2,300 and 10% for 2,300-3,200. SC6 at US$2,501-3,000 is 10% in every version; at US$3,001-3,200 it is 12% or 10% depending on the version. Open the schedule page of the gazetted PDF (ghtaxclub.com, uploaded 2026-04) to settle it; the Dec 2025 version may differ.

Ghana: L.I. 2517 defines no spodumene reference grade (value is set at arm's length against international prices). Copper royalty not found. Any option for the state to buy beyond the 10% free carry not found. The 35% CIT (Minerals Commission page, possibly 2023) and 8% dividend WHT (PwC) are from search excerpts.

Mali: gold and lithium TAV/royalty rates not established. Secondary reports conflict (Ecofin: price-linked 3-7% with gaps; Daily Beirut: 3-8%; DiscoveryAlert: 10.5%, possibly all-in). Decree No. 2024-0396/PT-RM (on mines.gouv.ml) and Law 2023-040 Title 8 are needed. CIT, dividend WHT, ISCP and local development levies not found.

Côte d'Ivoire: no excerpt states the 'above US$2,000' wording of the top 8% band. Copper and lithium royalties, CIT, free carry and option, and dividend WHT not found. The 2027 royalty increases (9.5% royalty, 3% local contribution, gold scale to 12% above US$6,000/oz) were pending in Nov 2026; check enactment before modelling production from 2027.
